extra.message: SQL Injection in Login — An attacker can bypass authentication, retrieve all user credentials, and potentially execute arbitrary SQL commands on the SQLite database. [verified: Code at server.py:102-107 directly concatenates unsanitized 'username' and 'password' from get_argument() into SQL query string. No parameterization, escaping, or input validation exists, enabling SQL injection via the login form.]

OS Command Injection in ServerHandler — An attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the server with the privileges of the web application process, leading to full server compromise. [verified: In ServerHandler.post() at line 125, the 'server' parameter from the POST body is directly concatenated into a shell command passed to os.popen without any sanitization or validation, allowing arbitrary command injection. The code path is reachable and no compensating controls exist.]

Path Traversal in StaticHandler — An attacker can read arbitrary files on the server, including the database file (test.db), source code, and configuration files, leading to sensitive information disclosure. [verified: StaticHandler concatenates user-controlled 'path' directly with 'static/' without sanitization (line 40). Using '../' in path allows reading arbitrary files relative to the server directory, e.g., '/static/../server.py' reads server.py.]

Path Traversal in ContentHandler — An attacker can read arbitrary files on the server, including sensitive data such as the SQLite database, source code, and system files. [verified: The 'file' parameter is directly concatenated with 'read/' and opened without any validation, enabling path traversal via '../' sequences.]

Reflected XSS in Search — An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the page, leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or defacement when a victim visits a crafted link. [verified: The SearchHandler passes the unsanitized 'q' parameter directly to the template (line 89) without any escaping or validation. The X-XSS-Protection header is disabled (line 88), and no compensating controls are present in the code.]
